scope: Post-screen closer-prior supplement, no changes to candidate46 registration, code or decision
title: ESOD: Efficient Small Object Detection on High-Resolution Images
version_evidence: Local extracted PDF header: arXiv:2407.16424v2 [cs.CV] 17 Dec2024
reread: Abstract, Figure2 and III-A decomposition into stem/neck/head and shared preliminary features. Earlier AdaSlicer/ObjSeeker reading is recorded in the existing prior audit.
overlap: ESOD explicitly reuses the detector's stem, slices feature patches, then performs later detection. Shared shallow extraction plus independent later patches is already a close small-object/high-resolution precedent.
difference_and_limit: Candidate46 asks whether the original independently resized five-view strong control can be retained exactly by direct atlas slicing. ESOD defines a different feature-slicing architecture; it does not guarantee equality to this project's independent crops. No positive novelty inference follows from this implementation distinction.
decision_boundary: Geometric failure already stops candidate46. This supplemental prior reinforces that generic feature reuse is not an unoccupied research contribution. No new accuracy or latency measurement.
zotero_status: Reused already downloaded PDF and its prior library provenance; no new import claimed.
